title: Control plane metadata compaction and hot-query path rewrite
creator: Sofia Nguyen
description: This ticket consolidates multiple cleanup and performance steps for the control plane metadata layer. Goals: reduce table & index bloat, eliminate slow polymorphic lookup patterns, and rewrite two hot query paths that drive control-plane API p95 latency under tenant-heavy workloads. We'll implement online compaction techniques, introduce compacted lookup tables (flattened polymorphic refs), add targeted partial indexes and materialized summaries, and deploy a safe backfill/rollback strategy.
context: Production telemetry (console and runtime) shows recurring p95 spikes from control-plane routes that join tenant_metadata, entity_refs and audit_logs. Large numbers of historical audit rows and wide JSON columns are contributing to IO amplification and index fragmentation. Prior work (ENG-11023 and ENG-14237) identified hot query hotspots and UUID migration constraints; this ticket operationalizes a safe compaction and rewrite with minimal downtime.
decisions: Adopt online chunked compaction jobs (golang worker) with tenant-bounded batches to avoid table locks
Introduce new table 'entity_lookup_flat' to replace polymorphic joins; keep original entity_refs for backward compatibility until rollout completes
Create partial indexes on (tenant_id, created_at) WHERE active = true for audit_logs and route_stats
Use materialized view 'tenant_hot_index' refreshed incrementally by trigger-based invalidation for high-frequency dashboards
Backfill done through sidecar jobs that write to new compacted tables then swap via atomic rename during low-traffic window
risks_and_mitigation: Long-running migrations could increase replica lag — mitigate with controlled throttle and read-only replica verification
Swap/rename failures could break queries — implement feature flag and gradual traffic switch using routing layer
Partial index plans may regress other queries — add preflight explain checks and a small A/B on internal staging
tasks: Schema: create entity_lookup_flat schema and migration script (non-blocking)
Worker: implement chunked compaction worker with tenant_id cursor and rate limiter
Indexing: add partial indexes on audit_logs (tenant_id, created_at) WHERE active = true
Backfill: build safe backfill that populates entity_lookup_flat from entity_refs + tenant_metadata
Query rewrite: update control-plane hot routes to use entity_lookup_flat with a feature flag
Observability: add dashboards for compaction progress, replica lag, p95 latency per route
Testing: run synthetic high-tenant-load benchmark, capture before/after explain plans
Rollout: staged traffic switch with canary toggles and rollback runbook
acceptance_criteria: p95 control-plane route latency for /v1/tenant/* reduced by at least 25% in the canary compared to baseline
Index bloat (pgstat or equivalent) reduced to <20% free space on audited tables after compaction
Compaction worker supports pause/resume and records progress per-tenant in a durable table
Entity lookup correctness validated via golden test harness and matched row counts for 100 sampled tenants
Zero sustained increase in replica lag during staged rollout (spikes allowed within defined thresholds)
progress_updates: 2025-02-11: Spike yielded migration plan and initial schema for entity_lookup_flat. Decided on chunk size 1000 rows/iteration.
2025-02-18: PoC compaction worker written; validated with snapshot workload on dev cluster. Observed 18% CPU uplift, controlled by rate limiter.
2025-02-24: Partial index DDL prepared and tested on staging; explain plans show reduced index scan widths for hot queries.
2025-03-03: Backfill dry-run completed for 50 tenants in staging; found edge cases where entity_refs had null tenant_id — created cleanup subtask.
review_feedback: PM (Asha Patel): prioritize low-risk tenants for initial canary and document communication cadence for affected customers
DBA (Rajiv Menon): recommend additional vacuum strategy and to run pg_repack on one-node staging before production
Security (Maya Li): confirm no PII amplification during compaction jobs; implement KMS use for audit export if needed
notes_for_oncall: If compaction job causes replica lag > 30s, pause worker immediately and notify DB team
Watch for query timeouts on control-plane-read routes during swap window; rollback feature flag if errors exceed 0.5%
Use read-repair script to reconcile entity_lookup_flat vs entity_refs if mismatch detected
